status: Pre-training research decision. Time, target and comparison rules fixed before model scoring. GPU-dependent batch/width/step budget will be recorded after a bounded pilot, before the comparison sweep.

data.scope: Released Yambda listen-user cohort; not a representative sample of all production users.
data.history: All released events retained. Each prediction sees only strictly earlier timestamp groups. Policy and RM consume the last 128 past item events; the main personal-frequency control uses the same context. A full-history personal-frequency control, if included, is separately labeled as using more context.
data.ties: Group by uid,timestamp; deterministic item-ID ordering within past groups is representational, not claimed ground-truth order. Never use members of the target group in its input. Repeat multiplicity is retained.
data.sft_target: For a sampled user and target-time group in train, predict a uniformly sampled in-catalog event of that group from the strictly earlier history. Group eligibility and conditional in-catalog loss are reported.
data.training_sampling: Uniform over eligible users, then uniform over their eligible target-time groups. Fix seeds and sample budget. RM uses the same history convention and only observed event labels.

time.unit: Native seconds since undisclosed origin; already rounded down to multiples of five.
time.weights_and_catalog: Fit only before train_end_exclusive and freeze thereafter. No final-test refit under this version.
time.evaluation_history: At each cutoff, use observed history strictly before that cutoff, then freeze it for the day's ranking queries. Earlier validation events can enter later query histories but not fitted weights/statistics.

catalog.selection: Most frequent train items; ties broken by item_id ascending.
catalog.repeat_policy: Allow previously listened tracks. No duplicate item within one ranked top-K list.
catalog.special_tokens: PAD, BOS and UNK are input representation tokens only, excluded from policy action support and ranking.
catalog.oov: Retain history event positions as UNK. Exclude unknown SFT target actions with coverage disclosure. Future ranking targets outside catalog remain in denominators as misses.

evaluation.ranking_target: Unique user-item pairs with played_ratio_pct>50 in the future label window.
evaluation.auxiliary_next_group: For each warm user with a recorded event in the label window, use their first timestamp group in that window as the target set (all observed items, without >50% filtering); context is the strictly earlier real history, capped at 128 events. Report NextGroup Recall@10 separately from the primary frozen-day protocol. OOV targets remain misses. Do not select models on this auxiliary metric.
evaluation.primary: Macro NDCG@10 among warm users with at least one future positive; this is conditional on activity, not a retention estimate.
evaluation.reward_queries: All warm users at a cutoff, regardless of future activity. Report the active ranking subset separately if used.
evaluation.reward_reporting: Distinguish policy-expected predicted reward from predicted reward of delivered top-K. Neither is observed counterfactual user utility.
evaluation.uncertainty: Paired user bootstrap for within-window comparisons. Repeat key RL run with a new sampling seed if budget permits; report that this does not measure all initialization/data uncertainty.
evaluation.margin_interpretation: Predeclared practical tolerance, not a property of the dataset. Claim preserved relevance only if the paired interval supports it; otherwise say inconclusive.

reward_model.inputs: Strictly earlier item history, candidate ID and train-derived candidate length/popularity if used. No candidate played_ratio_pct or current-event is_organic input.
reward_model.independence: Separate frozen parameters and embeddings from the changing RL policy.
reward_model.validation: Constant, item-mean and item-only baselines; history removal/shuffle diagnostics; macro and event-weighted error; duration/popularity/origin slices. Confirmation and test remain out of parameter fitting.
reward_model.interpretation: Predicts conditional response on logged listens, not click probability, unconditional utility or causal reward for arbitrary recommendations.

rewards.capped_seconds: RM prediction * min(train-median track_length_seconds,600)/600. Capped equivalent-seconds proxy; not total listening time including replays.
rewards.scale: No per-batch advantage standardization that silently changes reward/KL balance. Report empirical reward spread and achieved KL.

rl.primary: On-policy H=1 REINFORCE with action-independent moving baseline plus exact KL to the frozen SFT policy over valid item actions.
controls: Continued SFT matched by update/context count with actual compute reported
Frozen SFT with reward-based exponential reweighting for H=1
rl.policy_selection: On selection validation, prefer candidates within the predeclared relevance tolerance, then maximize predicted reward on all warm query users. If none qualify, report the frontier without declaring a winner. Confirmation is a one-time check; failure does not trigger tuning on it.
rl.h5: Required diagnostic on generated histories, not simulated user acceptance. Use item-only context for both RM and policy; do not fabricate future listening labels. H=5 RL training is optional after the core experiment.

resource_pilot.device: RTX3060 12GiB, Windows, Python3.11.9, torch2.14.1+cu126; CUDA smoke passed.
resource_pilot.decision: Measure data-loading time, optimizer-step time, peak VRAM and checkpoint reload. Set fixed run budgets before the sweep; no promised completion time from parameter count alone.

prohibitions_on_claims: Do not treat generated recommendation as observed user interaction.
Do not label unobserved items as known dislikes.
Do not call a relevance/reward mismatch proven reward-model exploitation without additional evidence.
Do not claim retention uplift or real user satisfaction improvement from these offline logs.
Do not compare old development-window scores directly with the new protocol.
